title: release-engineering-meeting-notes-2026-09-22
agenda:
1) Current release train status (v1.12)
2) Hotfix for tokenization bug (RINF-4821)
3) Changelog and customer-facing notes
4) Rollback and canary strategy
5) Next steps / action items
notes:
Quick summary: we are targeting v1.12 promotion to production next Tuesday 2026-09-28 pending final QA and canary metrics. Staging tests show 98.6% regression-free for critical e2e suites; remaining failures are non-blocking flaky tests tracked in RINF-4899.

Hotfix (RINF-4821): QA reproduced the tokenization edge-case that affects a small percent of requests when using sparse prompt inputs. Tomás created a minimal fix and opened runtime PR #2128. We discussed scope: patch only runtime tokenizer, do not roll new model weights. Marco confirmed we have capacity to run a focused canary (5% tps) tomorrow afternoon.

Canary plan: deploy hotfix to canary nodes in us-west-2 and eu-west-1 (5% traffic each), monitor latency P95 and error budget, run smoke tests + synthetic prompt set. If stable for 2 hours, expand to 25% for 1 hour, then full rollout. Automated rollback configured to previous image on >0.5% request error increase or >20% CPU spike. Priya to validate smoke tests and sign-off.

Changelog: Need final customer-facing text. Liam will draft the release notes focusing on bugfix description, impacted surface, and mitigation steps. Action: add note about tokenization hotfix and guidance for customers with custom tokenizers. Sana to coordinate publishing on release notes page and Slack channel #release-updates.

Rollback/Hotfix windows: agreed code freeze for core runtime merges at 2026-09-26 18:00 PT. Any PRs after that require release coordinator approval. We also documented fast-track criteria for critical fixes (security, data loss, major correctness).

Risks: 1) Flaky tests masking real regressions — prioritized to isolate flaky cases and disable for this train if noise is high. 2) Canary detection thresholds may be too permissive; Marco will validate thresholds with SRE runbook. 3) Timing pressure with enterprise customers on Reserved capacity — account managers notified; potential for manual rollback if customers request.

Misc: discussed small perf regression in sequence-length handling observed in benchmark runs (2-3% P95 increase at 4k tokens). Evelyn and Tomás to pair on profiling next week and propose kernel fallback if needed.
